elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 provides that “neither Party's total aggregate liability” may exceed the stated cap.

elements.element: The cap includes fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim as one calculation limb.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly references “fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap includes USD 1,000,000 as the alternative calculation limb and uses the greater of the two limbs.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 caps liability at “the greater of” the twelve-month fee amount and “One Million Dollars ($1,000,000).”

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 states that “neither Party shall be liable for any indirect ... damages,” subject to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 states that “neither Party shall be liable for any ... consequential damages,” subject to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its confidentiality obligations is an “Excluded Claim,” and the cap applies “[e]xcept for Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its data protection obligations is an “Excluded Claim,” and the cap applies “[e]xcept for Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its security obligations is an “Excluded Claim,” and the cap applies “[e]xcept for Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's indemnification obligations are included in “Excluded Claims,” which are outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's gross negligence is included in “Excluded Claims,” which are outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from wilful misconduct is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's wilful misconduct is included in “Excluded Claims,” which are outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from fraud is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's fraud is included in “Excluded Claims,” which are outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is uncapped for either party.
elements.evidence: A party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is included in “Excluded Claims,” which are outside the cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages subject to the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the Company's payment obligations, comprising all amounts due to HDI, “are not damages subject to such cap.”

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 applies the aggregate cap to “neither Party's” liability.

elements.element: The cap is equal to twelve months' fees.
elements.evidence: Although twelve months' fees form one limb, the operative cap is the greater of that amount and USD 1,000,000, so it is not strictly equal to twelve months' fees.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is carved out from the cap for either party.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are “Excluded Claims” and therefore outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap for either party.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality obligations is an “Excluded Claim” and therefore outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is carved out from the cap for either party.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an “Excluded Claim” and therefore outside the cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap for either party.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an “Excluded Claim” and therefore outside the cap.

result.reason: The added clause implements every preferred requirement: a mutual greater-of cap, mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, all specified uncapped carve-outs, and treatment of Company payment obligations as outside damages subject to the cap. It does not literally satisfy the fallback's standalone requirement that the cap equal twelve months' fees because the operative cap also has a USD 1,000,000 floor; this does not matter commercially because the preferred position is fully achieved. The redline is confined to the requested limitation-of-liability provision and leaves unrelated terms intact.
